rules.title: Individual consideration of criminal history
rules.requirement: Covered housing providers must not categorically deny housing to everyone with arrests or convictions and must consider applicants individually, subject to the policy's criminal-history exceptions.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to housing providers receiving DND funding and/or land, or having income-restricted units created under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy; the policy also applies through the Office of Fair Housing and Equity Affirmative Marketing Program. The criminal-history guidance excludes current criminal behavior and situations involving a direct relationship between a conviction and the housing sought and/or an unreasonable risk of substantial harm to others' safety. It does not govern where federal or state law imposes a conflicting criminal-history requirement.
rules.exemptions: Current criminal behavior; a direct relationship between a conviction and the housing sought and/or unreasonable risk of substantial harm to others' safety; conflicting federal or state criminal-history requirements.
rules.citation: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy, introductory provisions
rules.quoted_span:
Housing providers receiving Department of Neighborhood Development (DND) funding and/or 
land, or that have income restricted units created under the Boston Planning and Development 
Agency (BPDA) Inclusionary Development Policy will not impose a blanket policy that denies 
housing to anyone with arrests and or convictions. Housing providers will consider applicants on 
a case-by-case basis.

rules.title: Excluded criminal records in eligibility and eviction decisions
rules.requirement: Covered Developers/Agents must not consider arrests without convictions, convictions subject to judicial relief, juvenile records, or convictions more than five years old when determining housing eligibility or considering eviction. The policy excludes current criminal behavior and specified conviction-related safety or housing circumstances, and yields to conflicting federal or state criminal-history requirements.
rules.key_value: Convictions more than 5 years old excluded, subject to exceptions
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to Developers/Agents determining housing eligibility or considering eviction for housing providers receiving DND funding and/or land, or having income-restricted units created under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy; the policy also applies through the Office of Fair Housing and Equity Affirmative Marketing Program. Excluded records include dismissed charges, diversion programs and similar non-convictions; convictions subject to expungement, sealing, certificates for relief from disabilities or other judicial relief; juvenile records; and convictions more than five years old. The criminal-history guidance excludes current criminal behavior and situations involving a direct relationship between a conviction and the housing sought and/or an unreasonable risk of substantial harm to others' safety. It does not govern where federal or state law imposes a conflicting criminal-history requirement.
rules.exemptions: Current criminal behavior; a direct relationship between a conviction and the housing sought and/or unreasonable risk of substantial harm to others' safety; conflicting federal or state criminal-history requirements.
rules.citation: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy, paragraph 1(a)–(d)
rules.quoted_span:
1. The Developer/Agent (Agent) agrees to not consider any of the following categories when 
determining housing eligibility and or considering eviction: 
 
a) Arrests that did not result in conviction. This includes dismissed charges, diversion 
programs, and similar non-convictions. 
b) Convictions that are subject to a form of judicial relief, such as expungement, sealing, 
and certificates for relief from disabilities. 
c) Juvenile records 
d) A conviction more than 5 years old. Tenant selection policy related to arrests and 
convictions does not apply in situations where there is: 
 
 A direct relationship between a conviction and the housing sought and or unreasonable 
risk of substantial harm to the safety of others.  
 Landlords would consider additional factors such as: evidence of rehabilitation, the time 
that has elapsed since the conviction occurred, and/or the age of the person at the time 
the conviction occurred. 
 This guidance does not apply to current criminal behavior.

rules.title: Credit scores excluded from housing decisions
rules.requirement: A covered Agent must not use an applicant's credit score to approve or deny a housing application.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to an Agent approving or denying a residential housing application for a housing provider receiving DND funding and/or land, or having income-restricted units created under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy. The policy also applies to residential tenant selection through the Office of Fair Housing and Equity Affirmative Marketing Program.
rules.citation: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy, Credit paragraph 5(a)
rules.quoted_span:
a) The agent agrees not to use the applicant credit score to approve or deny housing    
applications.

rules.title: Credit history only substitutes for unavailable rental history
rules.requirement: Covered Property Managers may use an applicant's credit history only in place of unavailable rental history to determine the applicant's ability to pay rent.
rules.key_value: Only when rental history is unavailable
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to Property Managers considering an applicant's credit history for a housing provider receiving DND funding and/or land, or having income-restricted units created under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy, and to residential tenant selection under the Office of Fair Housing and Equity Affirmative Marketing Program. Credit history may be used only to determine ability to pay rent, in lieu of rental history when rental history is unavailable.
rules.citation: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy, Credit paragraph 5(b)
rules.quoted_span:
b) Property Managers may consider an applicant’s credit history, but such information may 
ONLY be used in lieu of rental history to determine an applicant’s ability to pay rent when rental 
history is not available.

rules.title: Evidence of ability and willingness to pay rent
rules.requirement: An applicant's ability and willingness to pay rent must be demonstrated through an identifiable source of sufficient income and prior rental history. The policy permits credit history to substitute for rental history when rental history is unavailable.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to applicants undergoing residential tenant selection by housing providers receiving DND funding and/or land, or having income-restricted units created under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy, and through the Office of Fair Housing and Equity Affirmative Marketing Program. The income and prior-rental-history demonstration is subject to the express permission for Property Managers to use credit history in lieu of rental history to determine ability to pay rent when rental history is unavailable.
rules.exemptions: Credit history may substitute for unavailable rental history for the specified ability-to-pay determination.
rules.citation: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy, Credit paragraphs 5(b)–(c)
rules.quoted_span:
b) Property Managers may consider an applicant’s credit history, but such information may 
ONLY be used in lieu of rental history to determine an applicant’s ability to pay rent when rental 
history is not available. Where insufficient credit is the basis for rejection, mitigating 
circumstances may include: 
 
 a representative payer or other reliable third party who would take written responsibility for 
payment; 
 evidence that insufficient credit was the result of a disability;  
 evidence that insufficient credit was the result of other circumstances and there is reason to 
believe that applicant will now pay rent promptly and in full. 
 
  c) An applicant’s ability and willingness to pay rent must be demonstrated through an 
identifiable source of sufficient income to pay rent and prior rental history.

rules.title: Lack of credit history insufficient for rejection
rules.requirement: A covered housing provider may not reject an applicant solely for lacking credit history; the policy distinguishes lack of credit history from poor credit history.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential applicants evaluated by housing providers receiving DND funding and/or land, or having income-restricted units created under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy, and through the Office of Fair Housing and Equity Affirmative Marketing Program. This restriction concerns lack of credit history, as distinguished from poor credit history, as the justification for rejection.
rules.exemptions: The provision distinguishes poor credit history from lack of credit history.
rules.citation: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy, Credit paragraph 5(c)
rules.quoted_span:
The lack of credit 
history, as opposed to poor credit history, is not sufficient justification to reject an applicant.

rules.title: Consider demonstrated higher rent burden
rules.requirement: A covered Agent must take rent burden into account when an applicant demonstrates a history of satisfying a higher rent burden than the Agent normally uses.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to Agents evaluating residential applicants for housing providers receiving DND funding and/or land, or having income-restricted units created under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy, and through the Office of Fair Housing and Equity Affirmative Marketing Program. The duty is triggered when an applicant can demonstrate a history of satisfying a higher rent burden than the Agent normally employs.
rules.citation: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy, Credit paragraph 5(c)
rules.quoted_span:
An 
Agent must also take into account rent burden if an applicant can demonstrate a history of 
satisfying a higher rent burden than the Agent normally employs.

rules.title: Care and prompt return of sensitive verification documents
rules.requirement: A covered Agent must handle sensitive or confidential mitigating-circumstance information with utmost care and promptly return all documents containing it after review. If the applicant refuses to provide or permit access to reasonably needed verification information, the Agent may stop considering that mitigating circumstance.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to Agents handling sensitive or confidential information in verification of mitigating circumstances under the policy's credit provisions for housing providers receiving DND funding and/or land, or having income-restricted units created under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy, and through the Office of Fair Housing and Equity Affirmative Marketing Program. An Agent may request information reasonably needed for verification, including confidential information; refusal to provide or allow access to that further information permits the Agent to discontinue consideration of the mitigating circumstance.
rules.citation: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy, Credit paragraph 5(d)
rules.quoted_span:
d) The Agent shall have the right to request information reasonably needed to verify the 
mitigating circumstances, even if such information is of a confidential nature (e.g. verifications 
from medical professionals that provide confidential information.). The Agent shall treat all 
sensitive or confidential information with utmost care and return any and all documents 
containing such information to the applicant promptly after review. If the applicant refuses to 
provide or give access to such further information the Agent may choose not to give further 
consideration to the mitigating circumstance.
